titulo: Venir + gerund = have been (doing) for a while
regla: Venir + gerund describes an action that started before now and has been building up until now (and may go on): Viene quejándose desde el lunes = he's been complaining since Monday. It often comes with desde, desde hace or a time phrase.

bloques.texto: The action **comes from the past toward now**: it started earlier and has been going on, gradually, up to this point.
Often with **desde, desde hace, hasta ahora, últimamente**.
Works in other tenses too: **venía haciendo**, **ha venido diciendo**.
Compare **llevar + gerund**, which measures the time: **llevo dos años estudiando**.
Tip: **venir** = it's been _coming_ this way for a while.

lista.es: ==Vengo pensando== que tal vez debería disculparme con Antonio.
lista.en: I've been thinking that maybe I should apologize to Antonio.

lista.es: Mi papá ==viene dándole vueltas== a ese asunto desde hace días.
lista.en: My dad has been mulling that over for days.

lista.es: En esa época mi hijo ==venía haciendo== cosas raras.
lista.en: Back then my son had been acting strangely.

lista.es: Los vecinos ==vienen diciendo== que hay que arreglar el edificio.
lista.en: The neighbors have been saying the building needs fixing.

lista.es: Sospecho que desde aquel día me ==viene ocultando== la verdad.
lista.en: I suspect he's been hiding the truth from me since that day.
He's been complaining right up to today.

lista.nota: **Llevar** measures; **venir** stresses the build-up from a starting point.
**Vengo corriendo** can literally mean _I come running_; context decides.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I've been noticing that you're tired._
In Spanish: _The company has been losing money since 2020._
lista.r: La empresa viene perdiendo dinero desde 2020.

lista.p: Which fits a measured duration? _Two years studying..._
